Examples: "Loyalty Program membershipNumber '123456789'", "Gym Membership membershipNumber 'M-98765'", "Library Card membershipNumber 'LIB-001'".

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: alumni
candidates.comment: An alumni relation between an educational organization or organization and a person who is a former student or member. Also called former student, graduate, past member. Examples: "A university's alumni include 'Jane Doe'.", "The club's alumni include 'John Smith'." Distinct from alumniOf, which describes the inverse relationship (person to organization).

candidates.label: alumniOf
candidates.comment: An alumni of relation between a person and an educational organization or organization they are a former student or member of. Also called graduated from, formerly attended, past affiliation. Examples: "A person is alumni of 'MIT'.", "John Doe is alumni of 'Boy Scouts of America'." Distinct from alumni, which describes the inverse relationship (organization to person).

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: hasCredential
candidates.comment: A credential relation between an organization or person and an awarded credential. Also called holds credential, awarded credential, possesses credential. Examples: "A person has a credential as a licensed engineer.", "An organization has a credential for business excellence.", "The professional has a credential in data science."

candidates.label: predecessorOf
candidates.comment: A lineage relation between a product model and its newer, often superseding, variant. Also called replaced by, succeeded by, updated to, newer version is. Examples: iPhone 10 is a predecessor of iPhone 11. Model A is a predecessor of Model B. The old software version is a predecessor of the new one. Distinct from successorOf, which points from a newer variant to an older one.

candidates.label: hasGS1DigitalLink
candidates.comment: A GS1 digital link relation between an offer, organization, place, or product and its associated GS1 digital link URL. Also called GS1 link, digital link, product link. Examples: "A product has a GS1 digital link for traceability.", "An organization has a GS1 digital link for its profile.", "The offer includes a GS1 digital link."

candidates.label: successorOf
candidates.comment: A lineage relation between a newer product model and its previous, often discontinued, predecessor. Also called "replaces", "evolved from", "preceded by", "derived from". Examples: "iPhone 15 is successorOf iPhone 14", "The new car model is successorOf the previous generation", "This product is a successorOf an older variant."

candidates.label: numberOfPreviousOwners
candidates.comment: The total number of previous owners of a vehicle, including the current owner. Also called prior owners, owner history count, past owners. Examples: "Used Car A numberOfPreviousOwners 1", "Vintage Vehicle B numberOfPreviousOwners 3", "New Car C numberOfPreviousOwners 0".

candidates.label: hasBioChemEntityPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a biochemical entity and one of its constituent biochemical entities. Also called composed of, contains, includes part, made of. Examples: "A protein has a BioChemEntity part of an amino acid sequence.", "A cell has BioChemEntity parts like organelles.", "A molecule has BioChemEntity parts of atoms."

candidates.label: spokenByCharacter
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a quotation and the character, person, or organization to whom it is attributed within a creative work. Also called "attributed to", "quote speaker", "character says", "uttered by". Examples: "The quote is spokenByCharacter Hamlet", "The dialogue was spokenByCharacter the CEO", "This line is spokenByCharacter a fictional narrator."

candidates.label: speakable
candidates.comment: A designation of sections within an article or webpage that are highlighted as particularly suitable for text-to-speech conversion. Also called "text-to-speech section", "audible content", "read-aloud section", "speech-optimized content". Examples: "The news article has speakable the main body text", "This webpage's speakable sections are identified by CSS selectors", "The speakable content is specified by a URL fragment."

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

candidates.label: sender
candidates.comment: The audience, organization, or person initiating and transmitting a message or action. Also called originator, dispatcher, message source, sender of message. Examples: `Email Message` sender `John Doe`, `ReceiveAction` sender `Customer Service`, `Broadcast Message` sender `News Organization`. Distinct from `recipient`, which is the receiving party.

candidates.label: knowsLanguage
candidates.comment: A language proficiency relation between an organization or person and a language they are able to communicate in. Also called speaks language, fluent in, understands language, conversant in. Examples: A person knowsLanguage 'English'. An organization knowsLanguage 'Spanish'. A diplomat knowsLanguage 'French' (fr).

candidates.label: hasOccupation
candidates.comment: An occupation relation between a person and their current occupation. Also called profession, job, employment. Examples: "A person has an occupation as a software engineer.", "She has an occupation as a doctor.", "His occupation is a teacher."

candidates.label: readBy
candidates.comment: A narration relation between an audiobook and the person who performs the reading. Also called narrated by, performed by, voiced by. Examples: "The audiobook 'Harry Potter' is read by 'Stephen Fry'.", "An autobiography audiobook is read by 'the author'.", "A classic novel audiobook is read by 'a professional narrator'."

candidates.label: utterances
candidates.comment: An utterances relation between a HyperToc entry and the text of spoken words or lyrics occurring within that section of a media object. Also called spoken text, lyrics, dialogue. Examples: "HyperTocEntry utterances 'Hello, and welcome to the show.'", "HyperTocEntry utterances 'We're going to talk about this topic.'", "HyperTocEntry utterances 'The sun always shines on TV.'".

candidates.label: agent
candidates.comment: An agent relation between an action and the organization or person who directly performs or drives it. Also called performer, doer, initiator, actor. Examples: "A 'write book' action's agent is 'John Doe'.", "A 'deliver package' action's agent is 'Delivery Service Inc'."

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.

candidates.label: byArtist
candidates.comment: A performance relation between a music album or recording and the music group or person who performed it. Also called "performed by", "artist of", "featuring artist". Examples: "Album 'Thriller' byArtist Michael Jackson", "Recording 'Bohemian Rhapsody' byArtist Queen". Distinct from composer, which is the person who wrote the music, whereas byArtist is the performer.

candidates.label: creator
candidates.comment: An authorship relation between a creative work or user comment and the person or organization responsible for its creation. Also called: author, originator, producer, made by. Examples: "Novel" creator "Jane Doe", "Software" creator "Acme Corp.", "Blog Post" creator "John Smith", "User Review" creator "Anonymous User". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which is about legal ownership.

candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

candidates.label: roleName
candidates.comment: The specific designation or title of a role performed by a person or organization. Also called role title, position name, function name. Examples: `Person in Movie` roleName `"Actor"`, `Team Member` roleName `"Quarterback"`, `Project Contributor` roleName `"Lead Developer"`.

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.

candidates.label: performers
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and its primary performers, who can be organizations or persons. Also called main artists, headliners, principal actors, featured performers. Examples: A concert has performers 'Coldplay'. A play has performers 'The Royal Shakespeare Company'. A festival has performers 'Various Artists'. Distinct from performer, which can be any performer, not necessarily the main one.

candidates.label: provider
candidates.comment: A provision relation between an action, work, program, or service and the organization or person that supplies or performs it. Also called supplied by, performed by, offered by, produced by. Examples: "A parcel delivery is provided by FedEx.", "A financial incentive is provided by the government.", "A medical service is provided by Dr. Smith."

candidates.label: agent
candidates.comment: An agent relation between an action and the organization or person who directly performs or drives it. Also called performer, doer, initiator, actor. Examples: "A 'write book' action's agent is 'John Doe'.", "A 'deliver package' action's agent is 'Delivery Service Inc'."

candidates.label: founder
candidates.comment: A founder relation between an organization and the person or organization that established it. Also called: established by, created by, initiated by. Examples: "Microsoft" founder "Bill Gates", "Apple Inc." founder "Steve Jobs", "Google" founder "Larry Page". Distinct from founders, which is specifically for multiple people.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: nonEqual
candidates.comment: A qualitative value that is not equal to another qualitative value. Also called not equivalent to, different from, unequal to. Examples: "Value A nonEqual 'Value B'", "Color Red nonEqual 'Color Blue'", "Size Small nonEqual 'Size Large'". Distinct from equal, which indicates equivalence.

candidates.label: sportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A specific location relation between an exercise action and the sports activity venue where it took place. Also called "exercise location", "training venue", "athletic facility", "gym location". Examples: "The run had sportsActivityLocation Central Park", "The workout's sportsActivityLocation was the local gym", "This exercise action took place at a sportsActivityLocation stadium.". Distinct from location, which is a more general location property.

candidates.label: spatial
candidates.comment: A general spatial relation between a creative work and a place, used when more specific location properties are not applicable. Also called "related to place", "takes place in", "associated location", "geographic context". Examples: "The novel has spatial Paris", "The painting's spatial is a rural landscape", "This document's spatial is the Amazon rainforest.". Distinct from spatialCoverage, which indicates the specific geographic focus of the content.

candidates.label: exceptDate
candidates.comment: An exception date relation between a schedule and a specific date or datetime when a scheduled event will not take place. Also called: exclusion date, cancelled date, unavailable date. Examples: "Weekly Yoga Class Schedule" except date "2023-12-25", "Daily Bus Route Schedule" except date "2024-01-01T08:00:00", "Monthly Book Club Schedule" except date "2023-11-11".

candidates.label: free
candidates.comment: A free relation indicating whether a publication event, item, or place is accessible without cost. Also called: no charge, complimentary, gratis. Examples: "Online Article Publication" free "true", "Concert Event" free "false", "Public Park Access" free "true".

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: isAccessibleForFree
candidates.comment: An access cost relation indicating whether a creative work, event, or place can be accessed without charge. Also called free access, no charge, complimentary access, free of cost. Examples: A public park has isAccessibleForFree set to 'true'. An online article has isAccessibleForFree set to 'true'. A concert has isAccessibleForFree set to 'false'.

candidates.label: gameLocation
candidates.comment: A game location relation between a game or video game series and a real or fictional place where the game or part of it is set. Also called: game setting, virtual world, game environment. Examples: "Grand Theft Auto V" game location "Los Santos", "The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild" game location "Hyrule", "Assassin's Creed Valhalla" game location "England".
